_readme: Site glossary for en/ (base seed copied from the kit; the terms agent fills terms/decisions per site). shared = WoowTech series names and chrome terms reused across the 13 sites; terms = Headscale/Tailscale domain terms (upstream wording wins); keepEnglish = never translate/rephrase; forbid = words the reviewer rejects. v2 adds the cross-chapter decisions agreed before the 12 chapters were translated in parallel: headings, data-nav labels, callout labels, table headers and recurring phrases. Existing v1 entries are unchanged and still win.
principles: Upstream English UI/docs wording wins (headscale.net, tailscale.com/kb).
Product names, CLI commands, config keys, file names, hostnames and placeholders stay verbatim; Chinese placeholders become <your-…> style.
US spelling; sentence case for headings, nav and buttons; Title Case for product and WoowTech series names.
Second person 'you'; direct, like a senior engineer onboarding a beginner; no 'In this chapter we will', no marketing adjectives, no emoji.
Callout labels are fixed: Concept: / Tip: / Warning: / Danger:; full-width punctuation becomes ASCII; 第 N 章 → Chapter N; 圖 N-M → Figure N-M.

shared.讀完這章，你會: By the end of this chapter, you'll

decisions._readme: Binding cross-chapter wording. If a chapter can render a phrase two ways, use the form here. Section headings keyed by section id; per-chapter h2 forms are listed in full because they must not drift.

h2_by_section.faq: <Topic> FAQ  (e.g. Install FAQ, ACL FAQ, Troubleshooting FAQ)
h2_by_section.steps: <Number> steps to <verb phrase>  — keep the Chinese number (六步 = Six steps, 五步 = Five steps)
h2_by_section.why: chapter-specific; translate the Chinese h2 literally, do not replace it with 'Why this matters' (that is the data-nav label only)
